deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 16% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 15% last year; 8%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 97% (3 years ago 87%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $97 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 118% (3 years ago 156%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $14.8B, up 8% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Inventory up 154% vs quarterly sales up 12% (days of inventory 10 → 22). Products may be building up unsold — a warning sign in chip cycles.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 8%/yr over 3 years and 6%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 33% vs a 5-year range of 29–33% (median 31%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $102.1B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($86.4B buybacks + $15.7B dividends) = 2.0% of the company's market value. Share count down 1.6% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $10.58, down 1% in 90 days (down 2% in the last 30); 4 analysts raised, 2 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $8.84, up 1% in 90 days; 3 analysts raised, 5 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 6 peers (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, DELL, QCOM): sales growth over the last 12 months 15% vs a median of 20%; operating margin 33% vs 26%; price/sales 10.8× vs 5.5×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest year vs a year earlier: Americas 41% of sales, up 11%; Europe 27% of sales, up 15%; Greater China 17% of sales, up 28%; Rest of Asia Pacific 8% of sales, up 18%; 1 smaller. Source: 10-K XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $96.6M, 100% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

note.headline: Apple's business is strong, but the 355.63 price sits above every value estimate

summary.thesis: Apple is growing sales and cash faster than before, but the price already assumes about 26.7% yearly cash-flow growth, well above what its record supports.
summary.decision: Long term: wait for a lower price. Swing: wait, because the stock is moving sideways and the data has no clear upside target.
summary.act_at: Revisit near 313.15 or below; watch support at 342.99–348.15

note.happening: Apple closed at 355.63, up 2.04% on the day. It was trading near 357.84 intraday (not a close). The latest quarterly filing (2026-11-03) shows sales up 11.72% from a year earlier, slower than the 16.6% growth two quarters ago. Analysts have cut next-quarter profit-per-share estimates by 3.7% in the last 30 days. News since the last note includes reported $50 'Intelligence Usage Packs' for AI features, mixed reported user reactions to the new iPhone Duo, an 8-K filing marked 'other events', and the next earnings report on 2027-01-28.
note.business: The core business is in good shape. Trailing sales reached 478.8B, up from 416.2B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 136.1B from 98.8B. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) improved to 33.01% from 31.97%. The share count fell 1.56% over the year, so each share owns a slightly bigger slice. Two points need watching. First, growth is slowing: 16.6% two quarters ago, 11.72% now. Second, the filings flag that inventory is up 154% while sales are up 12%. Unsold product can force price cuts and squeeze margins, so this is the main real business risk. The company holds 36.3B in cash against 80.1B of debt, a net debt of 23.4B. That is small next to 136.1B of yearly free cash flow, so the balance sheet is not at risk. The news mostly affects sentiment. The paid AI packs are a reported new revenue idea, though their size is unknown. Google's $30 Pixel Tag and Meta's Muse on Apple Watch are reported competitive moves in small product lines. Mixed iPhone Duo reviews are reported opinions, not sales data. A new risk about an investigation in the annual report is a governance concern. Its business effect cannot be measured from this data.

worth.text: At 355.63, Apple trades at 39.6 times trailing earnings and 33.6 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 10.8, against a peer median of 5.5, and sits at the 100th percentile of its own 5-year range, the most expensive it has been in that period. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 146.14 in the bear case, 226.4 in the base case and 313.15 in the bull case. Apple's own historical price-to-sales range gives 222.27 to 300.79. Every method lands below today's price. The gap comes down to one input: how fast free cash flow grows from here. The current price implies a starting growth rate of 26.7%. At 20% starting growth the value is 274.92. Only at 30% does the value, 402.47, rise above the price. Margins matter too. If operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 205.79. My fair-value range is 226.4 to 313.15.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow growth: the price needs about 26.7% starting growth, while 3-year sales growth has been 8% and last year's was 15%.

bull: Free cash flow jumped to 136.1B from 98.8B, giving plenty of cash for buybacks and investment.
Operating margin rose to 33.01% from 31.97%, so Apple is keeping more profit per dollar of sales.
Analysts raised this year's profit-per-share estimate by 6.4% over 30 days, to 9.4.
bear: Price-to-sales of 10.8 is about double the peer median of 5.5 and at the top of Apple's own 5-year range.
Inventory is up 154% while quarterly sales are up 12%, which raises the risk of discounting and lower margins.
Next-year profit-per-share estimates fell 2.3% in 30 days, to 10.58, and next-quarter estimates fell 3.7%.

levels.what: Today's close, above the top of every valuation range, so there is little room for disappointment.
The DCF bull-case value and top of the fair-value range. Below this, the price would sit inside the range.
The high end of Apple's own historical price-to-sales range, a second reference point for value.

longterm.why: The business is high quality (grade B), with rising cash flow and margins. But today's price already assumes growth well above the company's record, and earnings estimates are being cut.

swing.why: The trend is a sideways range with a flat 20-day average, and the data shows no resistance level to use as a target. The price is sitting at the top edge of the 351.43–355.38 support zone, so a risk-to-reward plan cannot be built from the levels in the data.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-28 are the next big test, mainly of inventory and the slowing growth. January options (2027-01-15 expiry, before earnings) price a 7.8% move, and estimates still being cut argue against acting early.

change_mind: A daily close below the 342.99–348.15 support zone would signal the sideways range is breaking down and make me more cautious.
A drop toward 313.15, with operating margin holding near 33.01%, would put the price inside the fair-value range and make a long-term entry worth reconsidering.
If the next report shows quarterly sales growth back above 16.6% and the inventory gap narrowing, that would support faster growth and lift the value toward the 402.47 shown at 30% starting growth.
